concerns.text: Task T029a states: 'Explicitly note this as a sanctioned exception to FR-005's primary option'. This violates FR-005 and Constitution Principle VI which mandate Benjamini-Hochberg (BH) as the PRIMARY method. The task description incorrectly frames the mandatory requirement as an 'exception' to be noted, rather than the standard implementation. This is a semantic weakening of the requirement.

Task T028a implements a fallback to 'Phylogenetic Signal-Adjusted Spearman' for N < 30. While the Plan mentions this, FR-004 explicitly mandates 'Phylogenetic Generalized Least Squares (PGLS)' without a stated N-threshold exception in the spec text. The task introduces a 'staged simplification' (Spearman for small N) that is not explicitly authorized in the FR-004 text, risking a silent relaxation of the phylogenetic correction requirement.

Task T029b implements 'Permutation-based FDR Sensitivity Check' as a dependency of T028b/T028c. FR-005 mandates 'permutation-based FDR correction (or Benjamini-Yekutieli)'. The task treats permutation as a 'sensitivity check' (secondary) while making BH the primary. This reverses the hierarchy implied by FR-005's 'permutation-based... (or BY)' phrasing if interpreted as the primary path, or creates ambiguity on which method is the 'real' deliverable for FR-005 compliance.

Task T031 handles N < 10 by generating a 'Descriptive Case Study'. FR-009 mandates fallback to species-level aggregation if >50% linkage fails, but does not explicitly authorize skipping statistical testing entirely for N < 10. This task introduces a 'silent constitution drift' by defining a new output mode (Case Study) that bypasses the statistical requirements of FR-004/FR-005 without explicit spec authorization.

Task T057 pre-filters features present in < 10% of isolates. While the Plan mentions this, FR-002 requires extracting features for the analysis. Pre-filtering before the correlation step (FR-004) risks violating the 'all features' scope implied by 'every extracted genomic feature' in FR-004, unless the spec explicitly allows pre-filtering. This is a potential semantic weakening of the feature coverage requirement.
